NoteTexAccessor::bibliography_keys¶

Back to Note TeX Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

TokenBatch NoteTexAccessor::bibliography_keys() const

Extract Citation And Bibliography Identifiers By Source Cell¶

bibliography_keys() extracts the identifiers carried by citation commands and \bibitem declarations. It is the right operation when the keys themselves matter: building a citation index, finding unresolved references, or comparing the references used by independently stored source cells. It does not return rendered citation text or bibliography entries.

The recognizer accepts \cite and letter-or-star suffixed citation commands such as \citep, \citet, and starred forms, with optional square-bracket notes before the required brace group. It also accepts \bibitem, including its optional display label. A brace group containing a, b, c yields three keys: comma-separated fields are split, surrounding ASCII whitespace is removed, and empty fields are discarded.

Keys retain document order and duplicates retain occurrence semantics. If a key is cited twice, both occurrences are emitted; call a later uniqueness operation only when multiplicity is irrelevant to the task. Commands with a missing closing brace or nested braces in the key field are not matches. This is a source extractor, not a TeX expansion engine or a BibTeX parser: it does not expand macros, follow included files, or read bibliography databases.

The result is a closed TokenBatch. tokens() is one flat rank-1 Text Note. offsets() is a rank-1 Int64 Note of length source.numel() + 1; source cell i owns tokens[offsets[i]:offsets[i + 1]]. Empty source cells and cells without a recognized command contribute no tokens and therefore repeat the preceding offset. This representation preserves cell ownership without padding ragged results.

Extraction does not mutate the receiver. It scans Text cells in flattened row-major order and allocates keys plus offsets. Undefined produces an undefined token Note and the valid sentinel offsets Note [0]. Bytes and native scalar dtypes reject before extraction.

Example 1: Lists, Optional Arguments, Duplicates, And bibitem¶

const auto sources = pluss::make_note({
    R"(See \cite{knuth84, lamport94}; \bibitem{turing36}; \citep[sec. 2]{knuth84}.)",
    "no references",
    R"(\bibitem[Church]{church36})"});
const auto keys = sources.tex().bibliography_keys();

std::cout << keys.tokens() << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[5], dim=1, numel=5, encoding=utf8)
["knuth84", "lamport94", "turing36", "knuth84", "church36"]

The repeated knuth84 is intentional: the output describes occurrences, not a set.

Example 2: Offsets Recover The Ragged Rows¶

std::cout << "offsets=[";
const auto offsets = keys.offsets().integers();
for (std::size_t i = 0; i < offsets.size(); ++i)
  std::cout << (i ? ", " : "") << offsets[i];
std::cout << "]\n";

Output¶

offsets=[0, 4, 4, 5]

The first source cell owns tokens [0, 4), the second owns the empty interval [4, 4), and the third owns [4, 5).

Example 3: Undefined Has A Closed Empty Offset Domain¶

const auto absent = pluss::Note::undefined().tex().bibliography_keys();
std::cout << std::boolalpha << "undefined tokens="
          << absent.tokens().defined() << " offsets=["
          << absent.offsets().integers()[0] << "]\n";

Output¶

undefined tokens=false offsets=[0]

Example 4: Native Integer Cells Reject¶

try {
  (void)pluss::note::make(std::vector<std::int64_t>{1, 2})
      .tex().bibliography_keys();
} catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "bibliography Int64: rejected\n";
}

Output¶

bibliography Int64: rejected
